schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.model-access-request-v2.v1
schemasAdded.role: The version two desktop request. It names an organization profile and a catalog epoch instead of a fixed provider profile.

schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.model-access-receipt-v2.v1
schemasAdded.role: Extends the version one receipt with the resolved profile, variant, catalog epoch, deployment inventory and resolved deployment hashes, the confirmed model identity, the model the provider reported, and a usage record with provenance.

schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.model-access-result-v2.v1
schemasAdded.role: The terminal result, split into two closed variants by request mode.

schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.model-stream-event.v1
schemasAdded.role: The ten normalized stream event variants published to the desktop over the reviewed model stream route.

schemaMajorNaming.constraint: native-codegen.mjs hardcodes evidence-event as the only /v2/ URL family and schema-lock.compatibility pins ["v1", "evidence-event/v2"].
schemaMajorNaming.resolution: Version two is expressed in the FAMILY NAME at schema major one. File model-access-request-v2.schema.json, $id .../v1/model-access-request-v2.schema.json, title sapphirus.model-access-request-v2.v1, wire discriminator desktop-model-access-request.v2. No second /v2/ URL family was introduced and the evidence-event pin was not edited.
schemaMajorNaming.consequence: The generated TypeScript root type reads SapphirusModelAccessRequestV2V1: the V2 is the family, the trailing V1 is the schema major. That is intentional and is asserted in check-typescript-bindings.mjs.

structuralDecisions.decision: The version two consent is a $def inside the request, not a fifth file.
structuralDecisions.detail: ModelContextConsentV2 drops deploymentHash, because the desktop no longer knows or chooses a deployment, and adds modelProfileId, catalogVersion, requestedVariantId, requestMode, and contextSnapshotId. Changing the profile, catalog epoch, variant, canonical output schema, context snapshot, or request mode therefore produces a decision that no longer matches the request it is presented with.

structuralDecisions.decision: The receipt carries the request mode and the support route together in one closed response lane.
structuralDecisions.detail: ModelResponseLane is a oneOf over StructuredResponseLane (requestMode structured_response, supportRoute model_access, canonical output schema mandatory) and StreamingChatLane (requestMode streaming_chat, supportRoute model_stream, no output schema representable). This is what makes the required receipt route mismatch fixture a real structural rejection rather than a comment.

structuralDecisions.decision: The result is a oneOf over the two request modes.
structuralDecisions.detail: A structured response with no canonical payload and a streaming chat answer that claims a canonical output schema are both unrepresentable.

structuralDecisions.decision: The usage record is a oneOf discriminated by usageProvenance.
structuralDecisions.detail: ReportedUsage (reported or estimated) allows null per category, so a category the provider did not report stays null and is never conflated with a reported zero. UnavailableUsage requires every category to be the null type, so an unavailable usage record cannot be read as a free call.

structuralDecisions.decision: Tool definitions reference a canonical parameter schema identifier and hash.
structuralDecisions.detail: A request cannot carry an inline provider-shaped parameter document, so a tool definition is not a smuggling route for provider payloads.

structuralDecisions.decision: Stream events reuse the receipt usage definition and the request tool-name definition.
structuralDecisions.detail: The stream and the receipt cannot drift on how usage or tool identity is spelled.

invalid.proves: A deployment name cannot be transplanted into a version two request.
A project endpoint and an API version cannot be serialized into a version two request.
The version two consent decision has no deployment hash, so a version one consent envelope cannot be replayed into a version two request.
A version two request cannot omit the catalog epoch. This is the structural precondition for staleness detection, not staleness itself.
A receipt cannot claim a streaming chat answer arrived over the structured response route.
An unavailable usage record cannot report zero tokens. A category that was not reported is null, never zero.
A receipt cannot hide which profile and variant actually ran. This is the structural precondition for substitution detection, not substitution itself.
A streaming chat result cannot claim a canonical output schema.
No stream event may carry a bearer token.
No stream event may carry a deployment name or a raw provider body.
A stream event sequence starts at one. This is the structural floor under monotonicity, not monotonicity itself.

notStructurallyExpressible.note: FND-011 named seven invalid fixtures. Four of them are cross-document or temporal comparisons that no single-document JSON Schema can make. Rather than shipping a fixture that appears to prove them and does not, each is recorded here with the structural precondition that WAS proved and the layer that must carry the real check.

cases.why: Staleness is a comparison between the catalogVersion on the request and the catalog epoch the support plane currently considers current. Both values are well-formed CatalogVersion strings; only their relationship is wrong, and a schema cannot see the other one.
cases.structuralPreconditionProved: catalogVersion is mandatory and pattern-bound on both the request and the receipt, and the version two consent binds it too, so a stale request cannot be silently re-pointed at a newer catalog without invalidating consent.
cases.enforcedBy: The support plane catalog resolver (FND-024/FND-025) must compare and refuse.

cases.why: Substitution is requestedProfileId not equal to resolvedProfileId across a request and its receipt. Both are valid ModelProfileId values in isolation.
cases.structuralPreconditionProved: The version two receipt carries requestedProfileId, resolvedProfileId, and resolvedProfileHash as required properties, so the comparison is always possible and a receipt cannot omit the evidence.
cases.enforcedBy: ModelResultGuards.ValidateReceipt on the support plane and the receipt verifier in crates/desktop-cloud.

cases.why: Identical in kind to profile substitution: requestedVariantId against resolvedVariantId across two documents.
cases.structuralPreconditionProved: Both are required on the version two receipt, requestedVariantId nullable to carry the profile-default case and resolvedVariantId non-null because something always ran.

cases.why: Ordering is a property of a sequence of documents. A schema validates one event at a time and cannot know what came before it.
cases.structuralPreconditionProved: Every one of the ten variants requires requestId, runId, and a sequence of at least one, and the streaming receipt lane records eventCount and finalSequence so the desktop can reconcile what it saw against what was signed.
cases.enforcedBy: The renderer stream reducer (FND-045/FND-053) must abandon a run on a gap or a repeat.

cases.why: Uniqueness of completed, refused, failed, and cancelled within one run is also a property of the sequence, not of one event.
cases.structuralPreconditionProved: The terminal variants are closed and distinct, so a terminal event cannot masquerade as a delta, and finalSequence on the receipt pins where the run actually ended.
cases.enforcedBy: The same stream reducer, plus the support plane normalizer that emits at most one terminal event per run.

commands.result: 36 schemas, 226 closed objects, 13 discriminator refinements, 1147 resolved refs (before the FND-013 compatibility family).

constraintsObserved: productionOptionalNullablePolicy fail-closed-v1: every nullable property in the four families is required-and-nullable. No property is both optional and nullable.
check-generated-bindings.mjs regexes /\bany\b/ across all generated text including doc comments. Every description in these four schemas was written avoiding the bare lowercase word.
No $ref in these schemas carries a sibling keyword. The repository has no in-body $ref siblings anywhere, and the vendored generators were not asked to handle one.

cargo-typify emits `if value.chars().count() < 0usize` for a string with minLength 0, which fails the workspace -D warnings gate through unused_comparisons. The zero minLength on model-access-result-v2 outputText was removed; a zero minimum length is a no-op in JSON Schema anyway.
